AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: The current treatment of leishmaniasis remains a challenge, especially due to the need for multiple painful injections, the toxicity of the current drugs against the disease, the lack of efficacy and, lately the drug-resistant.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To demonstrate the biological behavior of 3-nitro-2-hydroxi-4,6-dimetoxychalcone (CH8) in animal model of cutaneous (CL) and visceral (VL) leishmaniasis Methodology: In order to evaluate itsbiological behavior the CH8 compound has been radiolabeled with 99mTc using the direct reaction. Groups of animals infected with visceral and cutaneous leishmaniasis has been administered with CH8-99mTc (oral), and a biodistribution has been performed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: The oral administration of CH8-99mTc demonstrated a poor absorption, nonetheless the absorbed drug had an expressively uptake in blood and liver, the mainly infected organ in visceral leishmaniasis (VL). While, CH8-99mTc administrated by subcutaneous route showed a poor distribution and a significantly uptake in the left ear, which suggest a local effect in the skin. Additionally, the infection with VL and CL models did not change considerably the biodistribution profile by oral and subcutaneous routes, respectively.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The results suggest that CH8 is a promising candidate for the oral treatment of VL and for the intralesional treatment of CL, showing a proeminent local effect.
